atoms.text: Now Bella is going to show you around the upper course of some rivers.

instruction.text: Can you put together the definition of upper course? Select the sentence parts in the correct order.
We’re in the Peak District in England. Select the flowing water to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a stream. The water from a few different sources has joined together, so the stream is slowly getting wider and faster.

instruction.text: We’re back in the Alps. Select the fast flowing water to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a ravine. In the mountains, water travels downwards very quickly because it is so steep. The fast moving water erodes the rock and makes ravines.

instruction.text: Now we’re back in Africa, at the Blue Nile Falls. Select the falling water to learn more.

feedback.end: This is a waterfall. Waterfalls are created by fast moving water eroding soft parts of the river bed, which is the bottom of a river.

instruction.text: We’ve continued a bit further down the Nile. Select the side of the river we are on to learn more.

feedback.end: The side of a river is called a river bank. When the water is moving quickly, it also takes chunks of soil and rock from the bank and carries them with it.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Bella would like to inspect the bottom of the Blue Nile Falls. Answer Bella’s question.

atoms.a: “What should we wear to walk to the bottom of the waterfall?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>What should we wear to walk to the bottom of the waterfall</voice>

text: We will need good shoes to get to this part of the Nile because it is very remote. When we get there, we will find a pool created by the falling water.

feedback.wrong: Ballet shoes would not be very sensible to hike to a waterfall in!

instruction.text: Now Bella would like to find out what is in the water in the upper course of the Nile. Answer Bella’s questions.

atoms.a: “What could we use to see what is in the water?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>What could we use to see what is in the water</voice>

text: Correct! In the upper course, we might collect some soil or catch some fish. We need to watch out for the crocodiles though!

feedback.wrong: A football won’t help us find out what is in the water.

atoms.a: The upper course is where the river ends.
Ravines are created by fast flowing rivers eroding the rock.
The bottom of a river is called the river bed.
The upper course of the river normally has fast flowing water.
